# LaTeX interchange convention

<!-- Generated by `pnpm interchange:doc` (app/src/lib/interchangeDoc.ts) from the parser's real support.
     Do not edit by hand: CI fails when this file differs from what the generator writes. -->

This is the exact form a Word document must follow so that MathBlocks' **Convert LaTeX** turns it into
finished equations, equation numbers and cross-references in one pass, with no manual fixing. It is
written for whoever produces the documents (for example, a transcription of handwritten pages into the
thesis template).

## 1. Paragraphs

| What | Paragraph | Text of the paragraph |
|---|---|---|
| Inline equation | any (in the sentence) | `… the position $\pvec{r}$ of …` |
| Display, unnumbered | style **MTDisplayEquation**, alone | TAB `$$…$$` |
| Display, numbered | style **MTDisplayEquation**, alone | TAB `$$…$$` TAB `\label{eq:3.2.5}` |
| Multi-line, one number | style **MTDisplayEquation**, alone | TAB `$$\begin{aligned} a &= b \\ &= c \end{aligned}$$` TAB `\label{eq:3.2.6}` |
| Reference with brackets | in the sentence | `\eqref{eq:3.2.5}` → (3.2.5) |
| Reference, number only | in the sentence | `\ref{eq:3.2.5}` → 3.2.5 |
| Chapter / appendix marker | its own paragraph, right after the chapter or appendix heading | `\mbnumbering{3}` or `\mbnumbering{A}` |
| Section marker | its own paragraph, right after each section heading | `\mbnumbering{3.2}` or `\mbnumbering{A.1}` |

### Equation numbers: chapter.section.equation

- Numbers are **(chapter.section.equation)** — (3.2.5) in section 2 of chapter 3 — and
  **(letter.section.equation)** in appendices — (A.1.3). The equation counter restarts at every section.
  References show the same format.
- The numbers come from the markers, never from typed text: `\mbnumbering{3}` after the chapter
  heading, then `\mbnumbering{3.1}`, `\mbnumbering{3.2}`… after each section heading (appendix sections
  too: `\mbnumbering{A}`, then `\mbnumbering{A.1}`…). A numbered equation before its chapter's first
  section marker is an error in the pre-flight and is not converted ("missing section marker").

### Labels are the equation numbers

- Write the label as the number the equation has in the draft: `\label{eq:3.2.5}`, `\label{eq:A.1.3}`,
  and cite it the same way: `\eqref{eq:3.2.5}`, `\ref{eq:A.1.3}`. (Other labels — letters, digits,
  dots and hyphens after `eq:`, e.g. `eq:energy-balance` — work too.)
- Each label once per document. References may come before or after their equation.
- If an equation's computed number differs from its label (a section was added, an equation moved), the
  pre-flight warns; the reference still points at the equation (its bookmark), so it shows the right
  number.

### Other rules

- TAB is a real tab character (Word's Tab key), not spaces.
- Never type an equation number in a new document (`\label` gives it).
- Inside `$…$` and `$$…$$`: plain ASCII — straight quotes, `-` for minus, `'` for primes.
- One display equation per paragraph; nothing else in that paragraph except the TABs and the label.
- `\(…\)` is accepted for inline and `\[…\]` for display, but `$…$` and `$$…$$` are preferred.
- A literal dollar sign in text is written `\$`.

### Notation

- **Physical vectors:** `\pvec{r}`, index outside: `\pvec{r}_1`.
- **Frames (vectrices):** `\vectrix{F}` — a bold capital with an arrow; never with a subscript.
- **Unit vectors of a frame:** the frame's letter in lowercase with `\bvec`, index outside:
  `\bvec{f}_1`, `\bvec{f}_2`, `\bvec{f}_3` for frame F (bold, with a hat).
- **Dyadics:** only `\dyadic{I}` and `\dyadic{J}` (bold capital with an arrow), subscripts outside when
  needed: `\dyadic{J}_{c}`.
- **Column matrices:** `\cmat{r}`; **transpose:** `^{\T}`.
- **Bodies:** plain letters, no kind: `B_1`, `B_{a}`.
- **Indices:** written plainly, with no `\mathrm`, `\mathit` or `\mathbf`: `\sigma_{sf}`, `B_{sf}`, `x_i`,
  `v_{max}`. Whether index labels are drawn italic or upright is a setting of the document style
  (Word style → Document style), not part of the LaTeX; a forced look in an index is dropped on conversion.
- **No hand-forced looks:** write `d`, `e`, `i` plainly too; the document style can draw d, e, i and π
  upright (ISO 80000-2). A `\mathrm{x}` that is left in is kept, and Check style lists it.

Example (one chapter, one section; generic content):

```text
Kinematics                                                        ← Heading 1 (chapter 3)
\mbnumbering{3}
Position                                                          ← Heading 2 (section 3.1)
\mbnumbering{3.1}
The position $\pvec{r}$ of a particle in the frame $\vectrix{F}$ is given by \eqref{eq:3.1.1}.
⇥$$\pvec{r} = \vectrix{F}^{\T}\cmat{r}$$⇥\label{eq:3.1.1}            ← MTDisplayEquation
⇥$$\cmat{r} = \begin{bmatrix} x & y & z \end{bmatrix}^{\T}$$          ← MTDisplayEquation, unnumbered
⇥$$\begin{aligned} \pvec{r} &= x\bvec{f}_1 + y\bvec{f}_2 + z\bvec{f}_3 \\ &= \vectrix{F}^{\T}\cmat{r} \end{aligned}$$⇥\label{eq:3.1.2}
Equation \ref{eq:3.1.2} expands \eqref{eq:3.1.1} in the unit vectors of $\vectrix{F}$.
```

This gives (3.1.1) and (3.1.2); the references read "(3.1.1)" and "3.1.2".

## 2. What Convert LaTeX does

1. **Pre-flight report, before anything is written:** the counts (inline, display, numbered,
   references, markers) and every problem with the text around it, in document order — parse errors,
   unknown commands, duplicate labels, unresolved references, malformed display paragraphs, missing
   section markers, labels whose number does not fit the markers, typed numbers that differ from the
   computed ones. You choose: stop, or convert the valid items.
2. **Writes, as one Ctrl+Z** (a backup is made first for large documents):
   - inline equations as MathBlocks objects on the text baseline;
   - display equations as MathBlocks objects in the paragraph's own style (centred on its centre tab);
   - numbered ones with a number field at the right tab and a bookmark named from the label
     (`eq:3.2.5` → `_MBEq_3_2_5`; dots and hyphens become underscores, at most 40 characters);
   - every `\mbnumbering` as a hidden numbering marker (its paragraph becomes hidden);
   - references as cross-reference fields (Ctrl+click jumps to the equation); unresolved ones stay as
     text, highlighted, and are listed;
   - then every number and reference is updated.
3. **Re-running converts only what is left** (converted equations are no longer text; numbers continue
   from the ones already converted; references may point at equations converted earlier).

### Keeping numbers right afterwards

- **Insert section marker** (MathBlocks ribbon → Section marker, or Ctrl+K): for a section added later.
  Put the cursor right after the new section heading; the marker is prefilled with the chapter (or
  appendix) of the marker before it and the next section number. Update numbers then renumbers the
  equations after it.
- **Update numbers** renumbers every equation and reference, and lists references to equations that no
  longer exist (Word would show "Error! Reference source not found"), each with the text around it.

### Pasting into a document with MathType equations

A document can have one numbering scheme only. If it still contains MathType's equation numbers and
chapter/section breaks, run **Convert numbering** (MathBlocks ribbon → Convert numbering, or Ctrl+K)
before Convert LaTeX — Convert LaTeX refuses to add numbers until then, because new numbers would not
continue MathType's. Convert numbering turns MathType's breaks into MathBlocks markers and its numbers
into MathBlocks numbers, keeping each number's bookmark so every existing reference stays on its
equation; you choose "keep the existing numbers" or "renumber to chapter.section.equation" (a section
marker after each section heading, read from Word's numbering or the heading text), and see the full
old → new list and any problems before anything is written.

After that, new text may refer to the converted equations by their number — `\eqref{eq:A.1.3}`
finds the equation showing (A.1.3) — and new equations continue the numbering (a new equation at the
end of section A.1 becomes (A.1.4)). A new label that repeats an existing number is reported.

## 3. Older forms that are converted too

- Display paragraphs with a typed number — TAB `$$…$$` TAB `(A.1.3)` — get a number field instead of
  the text; the report warns when the computed number differs from the typed one.
- MathType-style notation is mapped to notation kinds:
  - `\mathbf{\overset{\scriptscriptstyle\rightharpoonup}{r}}` → `\pvec{r}`
  - `\vec{\mathbf{F}}` (capital) → `\vectrix{F}`; for `I` and `J` → `\dyadic{…}`
  - `\hat{f}_1`, `\hat{\mathbf{f}}_1`, `\mathbf{\hat{f}}_1` (lowercase letter with an index) → `\bvec{f}_1`
  - `\left[\begin{array}{…}…\end{array}\right]` → `bmatrix` (`( )` → `pmatrix`, `| |` → `vmatrix`)
  - a forced look in an index (`\sigma_{\mathrm{sf}}`, `r_{\mathbf{n}}`) → plain (`\sigma_{sf}`, `r_{n}`)
  - ℤ ℝ ℕ ℚ ℂ typed as characters → `\mathbb{Z}` … `\mathbb{C}`; Greek capitals that look like Latin letters
    (Α Β Ε Ζ Η Ι Κ Μ Ν Ο Ρ Τ Χ) are reported as a warning

### What Convert MathType writes (accepted as they are)

Every form below is what converting a MathType equation produces; Convert LaTeX reads each back to the same
equation (checked in the tests on every build), so text written by MathBlocks or by tools that follow this file
can be converted again.

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| Physical vector | `\pvec{r}` |
| Physical vector with a frame pair (relative to) | `\pvec[P/O]{r}` |
| Primed frames in the frame pair | `\pvec[B'/B]{\omega}` |
| Vectrix (frame) and its transpose | `\vectrix{F}^{\T}` |
| Dyadic | `\dyadic{J}_{c}` |
| Basis (unit) vector with an index | `\bvec{f}_{1}` |
| Column matrix, matrix | `\cmat{x}=\mat{A}\cmat{y}` |
| Rotation matrix (direction cosines) | `\dcm{A}{B}` |
| Left superscript (frame of a column) | `{}^{E}\cmat{n}_{3}` |
| Left superscript and subscript | `{}^{a}_{b}X` |
| Primes | `x''+y'` |
| Dot product, cross product | `a\cdot b+a\times b` |
| Fraction, root, n-th root | `\frac{a}{b}+\sqrt{x}+\sqrt[3]{y}` |
| Sum, product, integral with limits | `\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i+\prod_{k}b_k+\int_{0}^{T}f\,dt` |
| Stretchy brackets | `\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)+\left[x\right]+\left\{y\right\}+\left|z\right|` |
| Matrices | `\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}` |
| Accents | `\dot{x}+\ddot{x}+\hat{x}+\bar{x}+\tilde{x}+\vec{x}+\overrightharpoon{x}` |
| Over and under | `\overset{\leftrightarrow}{I}+\underset{n\to\infty}{\lim}x` |
| Functions | `\sin\theta+\cos\phi+\exp x+\ln y` |
| Text and upright letters | `\text{if }x>0,\ \mathrm{d}t` |
| Bold Latin and Greek | `\mathbf{F}+\boldsymbol{\omega}` |
| Number sets | `k\in\mathbb{Z},\ x\in\mathbb{R}` |
| Spaces | `a\,b\:c;d\quad e\qquad f` |
| Aligned lines | `\begin{aligned}a&=b\\&=c\end{aligned}` |
| Cases | `f=\begin{cases}1&x>0\\0&\text{else}\end{cases}` |

## 4. What Word does to typed LaTeX, undone before parsing

Smart quotes → straight quotes; en dash, em dash, minus sign → `-`; non-breaking and other special
spaces → space; manual line breaks → space; soft hyphens and zero-width characters → removed;
autocorrect symbols → their LaTeX (… → `\ldots`, → → `\rightarrow`, ⇒ → `\Rightarrow`, © → `(c)`).

## 5. Supported LaTeX (exactly what the parser accepts)

Anything not listed here is reported in the pre-flight as an unknown command and not converted.

### Notation kinds (preferred for vectors, frames, matrices)

| Macro | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `\pvec{symbol}` | Physical vector |
| `\uvec{symbol}` | Unit direction vector |
| `\bvec{symbol}` | Basis vector |
| `\vectrix{symbol}` | Vectrix (frame) |
| `\cmat{symbol}` | Column matrix |
| `\mat{symbol}` | Matrix |
| `\dcm{to frame}{from frame}` | Direction cosine matrix |
| `\crossmat{vector}` | Cross (skew-symmetric) matrix |
| `\dyadic{symbol}` | Dyadic |
| `\tens{symbol}` | Tensor |
| `\quat{symbol}` | Quaternion |
| `\frm{label}` | Reference frame |
| `\body{symbol}` | Body / region |
| `\T` | Transpose mark |
| `\diff{variable}` | Differential |

An index goes outside the kind: `\pvec{r}_1`, `\bvec{f}_2`. The transpose is `^{\T}`.

### Structures

| Write | For |
|---|---|
| `\frac{a}{b}` | fraction (also \dfrac, \tfrac, \cfrac) |
| `\binom{n}{k}` | binomial (also \dbinom, \tbinom) |
| `\sqrt{x}` | square root |
| `\sqrt[3]{x}` | n-th root |
| `x^{2}` | superscript |
| `x_{i}` | subscript |
| `x_{i}^{2}` | both |
| `\operatorname{tr}` | upright operator name |
| `\overset{a}{=}` | symbol over (also \stackrel) |
| `\underset{a}{=}` | symbol under |
| `\overbrace{a+b}` | brace over |
| `\underbrace{a+b}` | brace under |
| `\boxed{x}` | box |
| `\left( x \right)` | stretchy delimiters (\left, \right, \middle) |
| `\bigl( x \bigr)` | fixed-size delimiters (\big, \Big, \bigg, \Bigg and their l/r forms) |
| `\text{ for all } x` | text (also \textrm, \textit, \textbf, \mbox) |
| `x'` | prime (ASCII apostrophe; '' for a double prime) |

### Environments

- Matrices: `matrix`, `pmatrix`, `bmatrix`, `Bmatrix`, `vmatrix`, `Vmatrix`, `smallmatrix` — rows end with `\\`, cells are separated by `&`.
- Multi-line (one number for the whole block): `aligned`, `align`, `align*`, `gathered`, `gather`, `gather*`, `split`, `alignat`, `alignat*`, `multline`, `multline*`.
- Other: `cases`, `dcases`, `array`.

### Symbols

- Letters and ordinary symbols: `\alpha`, `\beta`, `\gamma`, `\delta`, `\epsilon`, `\varepsilon`, `\zeta`, `\eta`, `\theta`, `\vartheta`, `\iota`, `\kappa`, `\lambda`, `\mu`, `\nu`, `\xi`, `\pi`, `\varpi`, `\rho`, `\varrho`, `\sigma`, `\varsigma`, `\tau`, `\upsilon`, `\phi`, `\varphi`, `\chi`, `\psi`, `\omega`, `\Gamma`, `\Delta`, `\Theta`, `\Lambda`, `\Xi`, `\Pi`, `\Sigma`, `\Upsilon`, `\Phi`, `\Psi`, `\Omega`, `\langle`, `\rangle`, `\lfloor`, `\rfloor`, `\lceil`, `\rceil`, `\backslash`, `\infty`, `\partial`, `\nabla`, `\hbar`, `\ell`, `\Re`, `\Im`, `\aleph`, `\wp`, `\emptyset`, `\varnothing`, `\forall`, `\exists`, `\nexists`, `\neg`, `\lnot`, `\angle`, `\triangle`, `\prime`, `\degree`, `\top`, `\bot`, `\varkappa`, `\complement`, `\mho`, `\cdots`, `\ldots`, `\dots`, `\vdots`, `\ddots`
- Binary operators: `\pm`, `\mp`, `\times`, `\div`, `\cdot`, `\ast`, `\star`, `\circ`, `\bullet`, `\cap`, `\cup`, `\wedge`, `\land`, `\vee`, `\lor`, `\oplus`, `\ominus`, `\otimes`, `\odot`, `\setminus`, `\dagger`, `\ddagger`, `\uplus`, `\sqcup`, `\sqcap`, `\circledast`, `\diamond`, `\amalg`
- Relations and arrows: `\leq`, `\le`, `\geq`, `\ge`, `\neq`, `\ne`, `\approx`, `\equiv`, `\sim`, `\simeq`, `\cong`, `\propto`, `\ll`, `\gg`, `\in`, `\notin`, `\ni`, `\subset`, `\subseteq`, `\supset`, `\supseteq`, `\parallel`, `\perp`, `\mid`, `\coloneqq`, `\doteq`, `\to`, `\rightarrow`, `\leftarrow`, `\gets`, `\leftrightarrow`, `\Rightarrow`, `\Leftarrow`, `\Leftrightarrow`, `\implies`, `\impliedby`, `\iff`, `\mapsto`, `\longrightarrow`, `\longleftarrow`, `\Longrightarrow`, `\Longleftarrow`, `\uparrow`, `\downarrow`, `\rightleftharpoons`, `\therefore`, `\because`, `\vdash`, `\models`, `\triangleq`, `\nmid`, `\nless`, `\ngtr`, `\nleq`, `\ngeq`, `\nsim`, `\ncong`, `\nparallel`, `\prec`, `\succ`, `\preceq`, `\succeq`, `\subsetneq`, `\supsetneq`, `\nsubseteq`, `\nsupseteq`, `\leqslant`, `\geqslant`, `\lesssim`, `\gtrsim`, `\asymp`, `\approxeq`, `\longleftrightarrow`, `\Longleftrightarrow`, `\hookrightarrow`, `\hookleftarrow`, `\longmapsto`, `\rightharpoonup`, `\rightharpoondown`, `\leftharpoonup`, `\leftharpoondown`, `\updownarrow`, `\Uparrow`, `\Downarrow`, `\Updownarrow`, `\nearrow`, `\searrow`, `\nwarrow`, `\swarrow`, `\leftrightharpoons`
- Punctuation: `\colon`
- Large operators (limits with `_` and `^`): `\sum`, `\prod`, `\coprod`, `\int`, `\iint`, `\iiint`, `\oint`, `\oiint`, `\oiiint`, `\bigcup`, `\bigcap`, `\bigoplus`, `\bigotimes`, `\bigodot`, `\bigvee`, `\bigwedge`, `\biguplus`
- Functions: `\sin`, `\cos`, `\tan`, `\cot`, `\sec`, `\csc`, `\arcsin`, `\arccos`, `\arctan`, `\sinh`, `\cosh`, `\tanh`, `\coth`, `\log`, `\ln`, `\lg`, `\exp`, `\deg`, `\dim`, `\ker`, `\hom`, `\arg`, `\det`, `\gcd`, `\Pr`, `\lim`, `\liminf`, `\limsup`, `\max`, `\min`, `\sup`, `\inf`

### Accents, fonts, spaces, delimiters

- Accents: `\hat`, `\widehat`, `\bar`, `\vec`, `\overrightarrow`, `\overleftarrow`, `\overrightharpoon`, `\overleftharpoon`, `\dot`, `\ddot`, `\dddot`, `\ddddot`, `\acute`, `\grave`, `\mathring`, `\tilde`, `\widetilde`, `\check`, `\breve`, `\overline`, `\underline`
- Fonts: `\mathrm`, `\mathit`, `\mathbf`, `\boldsymbol`, `\bm`, `\mathbb`, `\mathcal`, `\mathscr`, `\mathfrak`, `\mathsf`, `\mathtt`
- Spaces: `\,`, `\thinspace`, `\:`, `\>`, `\medspace`, `\;`, `\thickspace`, `\quad`, `\qquad`, `\!`, `\ `, `~`
- Delimiters after `\left`/`\right`/`\big…`: `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `\{`, `\}`, `\lbrace`, `\rbrace`, `|`, `\|`, `\vert`, `\Vert`, `\lvert`, `\rvert`, `\lVert`, `\rVert`, `\langle`, `\rangle`, `\lfloor`, `\rfloor`, `\lceil`, `\rceil`, `/`, `\lbrack`, `\rbrack`, and `.` for none
- Accepted and ignored (size/style hints): `\displaystyle`, `\textstyle`, `\scriptstyle`, `\scriptscriptstyle`, `\limits`, `\nolimits`, `\nonumber`, `\notag`
